content: Your immune system can function more effectively with proper treatment. Tipranavir is a medication classified as a protease inhibitor, which is used in combination with ritonavir, another protease inhibitor, to enhance (boost) its levels in the body. However, it is important to note that tipranavir is not a cure for HIV infection. To reduce the risk of transmitting HIV to others, it is essential to take all prescribed HIV medications exactly as directed by your doctor. Additionally, you should use effective barrier methods, such as latex or polyurethane condoms or dental dams, during sexual activity as advised by your healthcare provider. Avoid sharing personal items like needles, syringes, toothbrushes, or razors that may have come into contact with blood or other bodily fluids. Before starting tipranavir, read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist and review it each time you get a refill. This medication is taken orally, usually twice daily, as directed by your doctor. Swallow the capsules whole, and always take tipranavir at the same time as ritonavir. It is crucial to adhere to the prescribed schedule for all HIV medications to achieve the best results. Do not adjust the dosage or stop taking the medication without consulting your doctor, as this could compromise your treatment. Common side effects of tipranavir may include diarrhea, nausea, drowsiness, dizziness, headache, or vomiting. Your doctor has prescribed this medication because they believe the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. As your immune system strengthens, it may begin to fight off pre-existing infections, potentially causing symptoms of those infections to reappear. In some cases, an overactive immune response may occur, which can happen shortly after starting HIV treatment or even months later. Changes in body fat distribution, such as increased fat in the upper back and abdomen or decreased fat in the arms and legs, may also occur, though the cause and long-term effects of these changes are not fully understood. Severe allergic reactions to tipranavir are rare, but the medication can commonly cause a mild rash. It is important to seek immediate medical attention if you develop a rash, as it may be difficult to distinguish between a mild reaction and a rare, severe allergic response. This is not a complete list of possible side effects, so consult your doctor for further guidance. Before taking tipranavir, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to sulfa drugs, or if you have any other allergies. This medication may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Tipranavir may cause dizziness or drowsiness, which can be exacerbated by alcohol or marijuana (cannabis). Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks that require alertness until you can do so safely. Limit your consumption of alcoholic beverages. In rare cases, tipranavir may increase blood sugar levels, potentially causing or worsening diabetes. If you have diabetes, monitor your blood sugar levels regularly and share the results with your doctor. Report symptoms of high blood sugar, such as increased thirst or urination, to your doctor immediately. During pregnancy, tipranavir should only be used when clearly necessary. HIV treatment can reduce the risk of transmitting the virus to your baby, and tipranavir may be part of that treatment. It is not known whether this medication passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor for advice. Drug interactions can alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Provide your doctor and pharmacist with a complete list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal supplements. Certain medications can affect the removal of tipranavir from your body, potentially impacting its effectiveness. Examples include apalutamide, macrolide antibiotics (such as erythromycin), and rifampin. Tipranavir, when combined with ritonavir, can also influence the removal of other drugs from your body, affecting their efficacy. If your doctor has instructed you to take low-dose aspirin to prevent heart attack or stroke, continue taking it unless otherwise directed. Tipranavir may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control methods, such as pills, patches, or rings, potentially leading to pregnancy. Discuss with your doctor whether you should use additional reliable backup birth control methods while taking this medication. In the event of an overdose, seek immediate medical attention. If someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. In the U.S., you can call 1-800-222-1222. While taking tipranavir, regular lab and medical tests (such as liver function, HIV RNA levels, blood sugar, blood counts, and cholesterol/triglyceride levels) are necessary to monitor your progress and detect any potential side effects. Keep all medical and lab appointments as scheduled. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store unopened bottles of tipranavir in the refrigerator. Once opened, the capsules can be stored at room temperature, away from light and moisture, but must be used within 60 days. Do not store this medication in the bathroom. Properly discard expired or unused medication as instructed by your pharmacist. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless directed to do so. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the medication is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
